If your car is E20 compatible, then why are some fuel tanks still rusting?

E20 compatible doesn’t mean rust-proof.

If your car sits parked for long periods with a half-filled tank, ethanol can absorb moisture from the air.

The risk increases when:
• Your car remains unused for weeks
• The fuel tank is frequently kept half empty
• The vehicle is parked outdoors in humid weather

E20 compatibility means the fuel system components are designed to handle ethanol blends. It does NOT mean the fuel tank is immune to moisture-related issues.

Most people negotiate the price of the car.
Very few think about who should legally buy it.

And that one decision can change the entire tax calculation.

An HUF, Hindu Undivided Family, is recognised as a separate taxpayer.

Separate PAN.
Separate bank account.
Separate income.
Separate tax return.

Now assume a genuine HUF business buys a ₹20 lakh electric car and actually uses it for work.

Electric vehicles can qualify for 40% written-down-value depreciation.

So the calculation could look like this:

₹20 lakh EV
₹8 lakh first-year depreciation
Up to ₹2.4 lakh tax impact at a 30% rate, before cess

Over five years, the cumulative depreciation can reach roughly ₹18.44 lakh, creating a potential tax impact of around ₹5.53 lakh at the same rate.

But this is not a loophole where you buy your personal car in an HUF’s name and call it business use.

The HUF must genuinely own the funds, own the vehicle, earn genuine business income and maintain proper records showing actual business use.

The HUF is also assessed separately and gets its own ₹4 lakh nil-rate slab under the current new tax regime.

The real lesson?

The car you buy matters.
But the legal structure buying it can matter just as much.

Where almost every modern diesel SUV is using AdBlue/DEF, the Tata Sierra Diesel takes a different approach! 🚙🔥

So, why doesn’t the Sierra need AdBlue?

The 1.5L Kryojet Diesel uses an EGR + Lean NOx Trap (LNT) based emission-control setup instead of relying on an SCR system that needs AdBlue. The LNT traps NOx and converts it during the regeneration process, so there’s no separate AdBlue tank or regular urea top-up required.

In comparison, diesel cars equipped with SCR inject AdBlue/DEF into the exhaust. The urea solution reacts with NOx and converts it primarily into nitrogen and water, helping the engine meet strict emission norms.

Basically: Sierra Diesel = NO AdBlue top-ups! 😎

Most of us still want to own a house. It’s just not the only thing we’re chasing anymore. For older generations, owning a house was often the one big goal, and everything else came after that. Don’t put a price on your life to save rent

If you or your kids are living in a PG or rented accommodation, check these 5 things before shifting in:

1. Never Take a Basement Room
Basements are the biggest death traps. During rains, there’s a sudden risk of waterlogging. In case of fire or flooding, the only exit gets blocked instantly, making suffocation the biggest danger.

2. Check for “Diagonal Cracks” on the Walls
Look closely at the walls on the ground floor or parking area. Diagonal (X-shaped) cracks mean the building’s foundation is settling or sinking. Such a building can’t bear its own load and may collapse anytime.

3. Avoid Buildings with Only One Narrow Staircase
During a fire, the staircase acts like a chimney, filling up with smoke first. If a 4-5 floor building has just one narrow staircase, it leads to stampede in emergencies, and most deaths happen from smoke inhalation, not the fire itself.

4. Beware of “Top-Heavy” Old Buildings
Many landlords add 2-3 new floors on top of 30-40 year old pillar-less buildings (that stand only on brick walls). The old foundation can’t bear this extra load. Such buildings can collapse like a house of cards even in a minor earthquake.

5. Say NO to Windowless or Box Rooms
PGs often partition one big hall into small rooms with no direct window. Zero natural ventilation means in an emergency, you can’t escape through a window, and rescue teams can’t spot you from outside either.

Don’t wait for the government to act, do your own safety audit. If your current PG has any of these red flags, consider changing your place today.

The post, shared without any caption or explanation, does not represent an announced formal US government policy. The map has also caused a diplomatic reaction. Iceland summoned the US ambassador after the country appeared under the American flag, with Icelandic officials describing the post as inappropriate.

The larger concern is therefore not that these countries have suddenly become US territory, they have not. node.text: This is brilliant by @bombayshavingcompany 💯
Ads on AI is the next big arbitrage in advertising!
Vaseline temporarily changed their name to Baseline for the funniest, yet smartest reason!

Do you know, one of the biggest mobile games in the world found dozens of other games copying them, and instead of taking any of them down, they actually invited all those players to switch to the original?

So the game is called Clash Royale. And because it’s been so popular for years, a lot of other games have copied it. Same kind of characters, same kind of gameplay, some of them even have a very similar sounding name.

Now normally, any company would just send legal notices and get those copies removed. But Clash Royale did something very different. They created a website where if you were playing any of those copycat games, you could take your progress from that game and convert it into actual rewards inside Clash Royale.

And honestly, I think this is much smarter than just getting them removed. And here’s why.

See, when you take a copycat game down, the game disappears but the player just moves to the next copy. But here, the copy can stay alive, and the player still comes to you.

And the reason this works is actually very simple. The thing keeping someone stuck in a copycat game is not the game itself. It’s the months of progress they’ve already built there. Nobody wants to throw all of that away and basically start from zero. And that is exactly what Clash Royale removed.
What are your thoughts on this campaign?

Apple just made an ad where their Mac mini grows a pair of biceps. And honestly, it looks nothing like an Apple ad.

So the ad is called “The Mighty Mac mini”, and it’s fully handmade clay animation. The Mac mini grows arms and legs and starts flexing. Then it turns into a race car. Then it takes off like a rocket. All of this is basically to show that the new chip inside it is faster.

Now, Apple has never advertised like this. Their ads are usually clean and minimal, with a product sitting quietly on a plain background and a calm voice explaining it. So a playful clay animation is a big shift for them.

But here’s the part I find really interesting. Apple is not doing this everywhere. They’re doing it only at the cheapest end of their lineup. The MacBook Neo, which is their entry-level laptop, got a similarly unusual campaign on TikTok. The expensive Macs still get the same serious, minimal ads as always.

And I think there’s a real reason behind that.

See, Apple’s usual style works beautifully on someone who already owns a Mac and is just choosing which one to upgrade to. But for someone who has only ever used an iPhone and a Windows laptop, that same style makes a Mac feel like a serious professional machine that isn’t really meant for them.

And that is exactly the person Apple is trying to convince here, because the cheaper Macs mostly exist to pull first-time buyers in.

Now, Apple can obviously never say the word “cheap” in an ad. That would damage everything they’ve built over decades. But clay and handmade things already feel approachable and low-stakes to all of us. So the format of the ad is doing the job that the words are not allowed to do.

BMW recently did something very weird. They started showing Spider-Man advertisements on their car’s dashboard screen. 

Now this was part of a tie-up with the Spider-Man film. And interestingly, BMW’s explanation is that this is not an ad at all. It’s just a fun thing with a film that they are a part of.

Now here’s what makes this so weird.

A few years ago, somebody from BMW literally said that a car screen is a private space and that they would never use it to sell ads.

And that’s the thing. No company begins by openly selling advertisements inside a product you’ve already bought, because that would get rejected immediately. It usually starts with something that looks small and harmless. Something that doesn’t even look like advertising.

But once it has happened, the space opens up. Everyone realises it is doable, and people start finding ways to make it happen.

And while this is still not a very common thing, it is a little scary. Because if a car’s dashboard starts showing you ads, what happens to road safety?

I think that’s worth thinking about. What do you think?

It feels like sunlight is coming in through a glass ceiling in the video, right? But it’s actually not!

The crazy part is, Shilpa Shetty has this in her house, Peyush Bansal has it in his home-office, and even Mukesh Ambani has it in his home.

This is actually the work of a company called SUNROOOF. They create lighting technologies that make it feel like natural sunlight is entering your room.

And that matters because older homes used to have courtyards, and open spaces - basically what we call ‘aangan’. But our modern homes feel dark with fewer and smaller windows.

So SUNROOOF is selling the feeling of natural sunlight in homes and spaces that no longer get enough of it.

Infact, they are now even making something called Sun Window, which looks like it came in a TV box. It can hang on your wall like a painting, and actually works, feels and actually looks like a real window!

Honestly, this is one of those products that makes you stop and think, how is this even real?

You remember when PM Modi gifted the Italian Prime Minister a packet of Melody toffees, and the whole thing blew up on the internet? So Parle, the makers of Melody, did something very interesting after that.

They turned that moment into an actual product.

It’s a limited edition Melody Tiramisu, which is basically a coffee flavoured version of the toffee. And on the pack, they’ve literally written “Celebrating India-Italy friendship”

Now, I think this is really smart, and here’s why.

See, moment marketing has always been about putting out a post or a campaign, getting the internet to enjoy, and being done with it. But this is possibly the first time, atleast I can think of, where an actual product has come out of a moment marketing situation!

And what makes it more interesting is the speed. Big legacy companies are usually expected to be slow and bureaucratic about this stuff. Parle is as legacy as it gets, and they still managed to pull this off fairly quickly. And I think that’s quite cool!
